transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Willow Care), Evan Ruiz (Willow CTO), Dr. Leah Kim (Willow Product)

Summary: quick onboarding kickoff, confirm success criteria, security requirements, and immediate action items for pilot.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're excited to get Willow Care onboard. quick intro from our side — I'm Jordan, i'm the AE...
[00:12] Maya Thompson: Hi, Maya here. thanks, and excited as well.
[00:18] Evan Ruiz: Evan — CTO. we'll be the technical owner on our side.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Priya, CSM at Redwood, i'll run the onboarding timeline and coordinate resources.
[00:29] Samir Patel: Samir, solutions engineer, i'll handle architecture and benchmark stuff.
[00:35] Dr. Leah Kim: Leah, product lead, focusing on clinician workflows.

[02:01] Jordan Lee: Cool, agenda for today is onboarding timeline, SSO and compliance, integration options (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private), and sample data ingestion. we'll wrap with next steps. anything to add?
[02:15] Maya Thompson: That covers it. main blockers for us are SSO and data residency — we need SOC2 level logs and a KMS integration for keys.
[02:32] Evan Ruiz: also cost predictability. we want to understand if Dedicated gives better unit economics for our expected throughput.

[05:00] Samir Patel: quick note on Dedicated — typically predictable throughput and isolation, autoscaling policies, you can reserve GPU pools. there's a tradeoff: hosting model on Redwood Hosted is faster to start but you get less isolation.
[05:18] Maya Thompson: right, that's what we wanted to hear. any docs on encryption at rest and HSM/KMS?
[05:25] Priya Nair: yes, i'll share our security pack after the call — includes SOC2 audit summary, KMS integration notes, and network diagrams for VPC/private deploys.

[08:40] Evan Ruiz: for SSO we use Okta, so SAML and SCIM are required. Do you support IdP-initiated flows?
[08:55] Samir Patel: yes, we support SAML SSO and provisioning with SCIM. there's a tiny setup piece on our side, we'll need the SP metadata and your admin contact.
[09:10] Dr. Leah Kim: and for role-based access control, we need separate roles for product, engineering, and compliance.
[09:22] Priya Nair: we can map groups from SCIM to RBAC in the console, we'll document recommended role templates.

[12:00] Jordan Lee: success criteria — what would success look like for the first 8 weeks?
[12:08] Maya Thompson: a pilot ingesting anonymized clinical notes, embedding search working, and latency under 300ms p50 for interactive features.
[12:20] Evan Ruiz: also an internal runbook for failover and cost estimates for monthly run rate.
[12:30] Samir Patel: we'll plan bench tests for p50/p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens, and share a template for results.

[15:05] Dr. Leah Kim: slight concern about model hallucinations in clinical context — do you have quality monitoring?
[15:16] Samir Patel: yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets and evals. we can run a small eval set against the model before the pilot.
[15:28] Maya Thompson: good, we'll prepare eval prompts.

[18:00] Jordan Lee: on ingestion, what formats do you accept?
[18:08] Samir Patel: common formats — JSONL, Parquet, and direct API streaming. for KV cache and prefix cache we recommend splitting by session id.
[18:22] Evan Ruiz: we use a message bus and S3 landing zone, will that fit?
[18:30] Samir Patel: yes, S3 ingestion and streaming from a message bus both supported. we'll include an example pipeline in the runbook.

[22:45] Maya Thompson: data residency question — our PHI must stay in-region. do you support region pinning or private deployment?
[22:58] Priya Nair: yes, Private deployment with a customer-managed VPC or on-prem option is available; otherwise we can pin hosted capacity to a specific cloud region for many customers. we'll highlight options and compliance tradeoffs in the doc pack.

[26:10] Jordan Lee: timeline proposal — Phase 1 (week 1-2) SSO + security review; Phase 2 (week 3-4) ingestion + pilot; Phase 3 (week 5-8) pilot validation and handoff. Does that map to your expectations?
[26:25] Evan Ruiz: that seems reasonable, we'd like the architecture workshop in week 1 if possible.
[26:33] Samir Patel: i'll coordinate that — propose Wed or Thu next week, i'll send a Doodle.

[30:00] Dr. Leah Kim: one more question on model variants and fallbacks — can you route by policy if a model is slow or to save cost?
[30:12] Samir Patel: yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible variants and route by latency/cost/region, you can configure policies per route.
[30:25] Maya Thompson: perfect. and about cost — any rough numbers for reserved Dedicated vs hosted per token?
[30:33] Jordan Lee: i'll put together a side-by-side. for a rough sense, Dedicated generally lowers per-token cost at higher throughput; hosted is higher per-token but no infra ops. i'll email an initial pricing sheet.

[35:40] Evan Ruiz: SLA and monitoring — do you provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards?
[35:50] Priya Nair: yes, Redwood Console has per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks, error analysis and token-level cost breakdowns. plus we can enable extended retention as an add-on for audits.

[38:10] Jordan Lee: closing — recap of action items: Priya share security pack and runbook; Samir schedule arch workshop and send benchmark template; Jordan share pricing and Dedicated vs Hosted comparison; Maya provide sample data and eval prompts.
[38:30] Maya Thompson: thanks, we'll aim to get the files to you this week.
[38:40] Dr. Leah Kim: thanks everyone, excited to get started.
[38:46] Jordan Lee: great, we'll follow up via email and send calendar invites. talk soon.

References: onboarding runbook link (to be shared), security pack (will be shared), benchmark template (Samir to send).

End of transcript.
